finding: The root package.json `customElements` field points to a worktree path `.worktrees/feature-healthba-hx-carousel-document-25/packages/hx-library/custom-elements.json` that will not exist on CI or any collaborator's machine, and is semantically meaningless at the root workspace level.
recommendation: Remove the `customElements` field from the root package.json entirely — it belongs only in packages/hx-library/package.json where it already correctly points to `custom-elements.json`.

finding: Root package.json uses `"name": "wc-2026"` which is a stale placeholder that predates the HELiX rebrand; the package description is correct (`@helixui` ecosystem) but the `name` field creates confusion in Turborepo task filtering and error messages.
recommendation: Update `"name"` to `"helix-monorepo"` or `"@helixui/monorepo"` to match the published package scope and avoid any future registry collision.

finding: pnpm-workspace.yaml correctly enumerates `apps/*`, `apps/mcp-servers/*`, and `packages/*` — all workspace packages are captured with a single glob per tier with no overlapping or missing entries.

MCP server apps live under `apps/mcp-servers/*` which is a legitimate location, but they are not surfaced in pnpm filter aliases or Turborepo `--filter` shortcuts in the root scripts; `build:mcp-servers` is hand-coded with four explicit `--filter` flags instead of a single glob.
recommendation: Add `pnpm run build:mcp-servers` to use `pnpm --filter='./apps/mcp-servers/**' run build` to avoid manual maintenance when new MCP servers are added.

finding: The `turbo.json` `test` task lists `.cache/test-results.json` as its only output, but Vitest actually writes coverage data to `.cache/coverage/` — Turborepo will cache the task without capturing coverage artifacts, causing stale coverage reads on cache hits.
recommendation: Add `".cache/coverage/**"` to the `test` task outputs array so Turborepo invalidates the cache when coverage data changes and consumers of `check-coverage.mjs` receive fresh data.

finding: The `generate` task in turbo.json declares `outputs` as `"packages/hx-react/src/components/**"` but this is an absolute path from the repo root rather than a path relative to the package — Turborepo outputs are resolved relative to the package root, making this output declaration a no-op that defeats caching for the React wrapper generator.
recommendation: Move the `generate` task into the `hx-react` package-level `turbo.json` (or scope it) and set outputs to `"src/components/**"` so caching is correctly scoped to the package.

finding: The `storybook:dev` and `storybook:build` tasks use a non-standard naming scheme (`storybook:dev`, `storybook:build`) that diverges from Turborepo convention; the root scripts `dev:storybook` calls `turbo dev --filter=@helixui/storybook` which maps to the package `dev` script, but `storybook:build` is not reachable via `turbo build`.
recommendation: Rename `storybook:dev` and `storybook:build` in turbo.json to `dev` and `build` at the storybook package level, or add an explicit Turborepo filter invocation in the root scripts. Verify no pipeline logic depends on the colon-namespaced tasks.

finding: The `lint` task declares `dependsOn: ["^build"]` which means linting any package first triggers a full transitive build of its dependencies — a >30 second operation that violates the design principle of fast lint feedback.
recommendation: Remove `dependsOn: ["^build"]` from the `lint` task; ESLint operates on source files directly and does not require a compiled dependency to be present. Use `env` inputs or `globalDependencies` if token type resolution is needed.

finding: The `type-check` task depends on `^build` (transitive build of all workspace dependencies) which is correct for accuracy but dramatically increases cold-start type-check time; there is no `inputs` declaration so any file change in the entire workspace invalidates the type-check cache.
recommendation: Add `"inputs"` to the `type-check` task scoped to `["src/**/*.ts", "tsconfig*.json"]` so the cache is only invalidated when TypeScript source or config changes, not when other workspace artifacts change.

finding: The `build` task correctly declares `dependsOn: ["^build"]` with comprehensive outputs covering all build artifact directories (`dist/**`, `build/**`, `.astro/**`, `.next/**`), enabling reliable incremental Turborepo builds across all packages and apps.

The `cem` task correctly declares `dependsOn: ["^build"]` and `outputs: ["custom-elements.json"]`, and `generate` correctly depends on `["^cem"]`, establishing the correct build → CEM → React-wrapper code generation pipeline ordering.

The `hx-library` tsconfig declares `composite: true` and a reference to `../hx-tokens`, which is correct for TypeScript project references. However, the `hx-react` tsconfig does NOT declare `composite: true` and has no `references` entry pointing to `@helixui/library`, breaking the incremental build chain for React wrappers.
recommendation: Add `"composite": true` to `packages/hx-react/tsconfig.json` and add `"references": [{"path": "../hx-library"}]` so TypeScript project references are honored across the entire package graph.

finding: The MCP server tsconfigs (e.g., `apps/mcp-servers/health-scorer/tsconfig.json`) override `module` to `Node16` and `moduleResolution` to `Node16` which conflicts with the base config's `moduleResolution: bundler` and `module: ESNext` — these extensions partially override tsconfig.base.json while silently losing other base settings because `extends` merges rather than replaces.
recommendation: Audit all MCP server tsconfigs to ensure they explicitly re-declare all options that differ from the base, or maintain a separate `tsconfig.node.json` base for Node16/CommonJS targets to avoid silent inheritance conflicts.

finding: tsconfig.base.json enforces `strict: true`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess: true`, `exactOptionalPropertyTypes: true`, `isolatedModules: true`, and `forceConsistentCasingInFileNames: true` — this is an exceptionally thorough strict configuration that protects against the most common runtime type errors.

The `apps/admin/tsconfig.json` does NOT extend `../../tsconfig.base.json` — it duplicates base settings manually and is missing `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, and `isolatedModules` from the shared strict config, creating a weaker type-safety guarantee in the admin app versus the library.
recommendation: Change admin tsconfig to `"extends": "../../tsconfig.base.json"` and add only admin-specific overrides (`jsx: preserve`, `incremental: true`, Next.js plugin) to restore full strict mode parity.

finding: The `src/index.ts` barrel is auto-generated by `scripts/generate-barrel.js` and run as `prepare` and `prebuild` hooks, eliminating merge conflicts on the barrel file across concurrent PRs — this is a well-designed solution for large multi-component monorepos.

The barrel `src/index.ts` contains inline `export { A, B } from './components/hx-foo/index.js'` and separate `export type { X }` lines from the same component index rather than grouping them, resulting in multiple import statements per component in the generated barrel — a consumer bundler will deduplicate these but static analysis tools and TypeScript language server may show redundant module resolution entries.
recommendation: Refactor the barrel generator to emit combined `export { Value, type SomeType }` statements per component (TypeScript 5.x supports inline type exports) to reduce per-component barrel lines from 2–3 to 1.

finding: The library barrel imports `./utilities/document-token-adoption.js` as a side-effect at the top of `index.ts`, ensuring token adoption runs once on any import of `@helixui/library`, which is the correct pattern for adopted stylesheets with Shadow DOM — well aligned with the project's stated adopted-stylesheets-as-default directive.

The `hx-react` package `src/index.ts` is auto-generated from CEM but is committed to version control (Git-tracked) — any CEM regeneration that adds or removes a component will produce a diff that must be committed separately, creating a two-step workflow (generate then commit) that agents have historically forgotten to do, leading to stale wrapper exports.
recommendation: Add `packages/hx-react/src/` to `.gitignore` and treat it as fully generated output, or add a CI check that runs `pnpm --filter=@helixui/react generate` and asserts `git diff --exit-code packages/hx-react/src/` to detect stale wrappers before merge.

finding: The `hx-library` package.json has a correct and complete exports map covering the root entry point, per-component deep imports (`./components/*`), the CEM JSON file, FOUC CSS, and all named CSS bundle paths — all with paired `types` and `import` conditions.

The `sideEffects` array in `hx-library/package.json` includes both `./dist/components/*/index.js` and `./src/components/*/index.ts` — the `src/` paths are never in the published `files` array and will never exist in a consumer's `node_modules`, so this is dead configuration that adds noise without protection.
recommendation: Remove the `./src/components/*/index.ts` and `./src/utilities/document-token-adoption.ts` entries from `sideEffects`; only `dist/` paths and `**/*.css` need to be marked.

finding: `packages/drupal-behaviors/package.json` uses `"main": "src/index.js"` with no `exports` map and no `types` field — this package has no TypeScript declarations, no ESM exports map, and references source files as the published entry point. A consumer importing `@helixui/drupal-behaviors` in a TypeScript project gets no types and will hit `src/` source rather than compiled output.
recommendation: Add a `build` script, `"exports"` map with `types` and `import` conditions, compile the package to `dist/`, and update `"main"` and `"files"` accordingly to match the patterns established in `hx-library`.

finding: `packages/drupal-starter/package.json` has no `main`, `types`, or `exports` field at all, and no `build` or `type-check` script — this package is effectively untyped and unbuildable through the Turborepo pipeline, relying entirely on its `files` array of raw source directories.
recommendation: Either explicitly mark this package as a non-JS asset bundle (remove it from TypeScript tooling) or add proper `exports`, `build`, and `type-check` scripts consistent with the rest of the workspace.

finding: The `hx-react` package.json has both `"main"` and `"module"` fields pointing to the same `./dist/index.js` — the `module` field is a Webpack-era convention not recognized by Node.js or standard bundlers that use the `exports` map, and creates confusion since the `exports` map (which takes precedence) already specifies the correct ESM entry.
recommendation: Remove the redundant `"module"` field from `packages/hx-react/package.json` since the `exports` map covers all modern bundler resolution paths.

finding: The `hx-react` package specifies `"react": "^18.3.1"` in `dependencies` (not `peerDependencies`) while simultaneously declaring it in `peerDependencies` — this double-declaration will cause React to be bundled in the output for consumers who already have React, and may trigger duplicate React instance errors in applications.
recommendation: Remove `react` from `hx-react` `dependencies` entirely; it belongs only in `peerDependencies`. `@lit/react` must remain in `dependencies` as it is a runtime requirement.

finding: The `hx-react` `peerDependencies` requires `react-dom >= 18.0.0` but `react-dom` is never actually imported in the wrapper components (they are Lit custom elements, not React DOM components) — this is a ghost peer dependency that will trigger unnecessary peer resolution warnings in consuming projects.
recommendation: Remove `react-dom` from `peerDependencies` in `packages/hx-react/package.json` unless a specific import of `react-dom` or `react-dom/client` is present in the wrapper source.

finding: Changesets are correctly configured with `linked: [["@helixui/library", "@helixui/tokens"]]` which ensures library and tokens versions stay in sync — critical for consumers who must use matching token and component versions.

The changeset `baseBranch` is set to `main` but the actual development flow routes through `dev` → `staging` → `main`; features land on `dev` first, and changeset CLI will compute diffs against `main` rather than `dev`, causing the changeset to undercount changed packages on a feature branch that has not yet promoted.
recommendation: Change `"baseBranch": "dev"` in `.changeset/config.json` to match the actual branch that all feature work targets, or ensure changeset generation is always done after merging to `dev`.

finding: The `@helixui/react` package is NOT in the `ignore` list and NOT in the `linked` group — React wrappers are auto-generated from the library CEM but will need independent changeset entries, creating a versioning mismatch risk where `@helixui/react` lags behind `@helixui/library` releases.
recommendation: Add `@helixui/react` to the `linked` group alongside `@helixui/library` and `@helixui/tokens`, or add it to `ignore` with a note that React wrapper versions are managed by the generation pipeline.

finding: The `scripts/preflight.sh` implements a comprehensive 9-gate local CI equivalent with smart diff detection, a stale-output watchdog for Vitest browser mode hangs, correct gate numbering commentary, and meaningful bypass env vars (`SKIP_ACT=1`, `SKIP_CHANGESET=1`) — this is production-grade scripting.

In `scripts/preflight.sh`, gate numbering in the UI output is inconsistent: coverage check runs between gates 5 and 6 without a numbered label, and the Storybook gate is labeled `[7.5/9]` — this creates confusion when auditing gate failures from CI logs or communicating failures to team members.
recommendation: Renumber the gates sequentially (1–10 if needed) and give the coverage check and Storybook check their own numbered labels so every gate has an unambiguous identifier in log output.

finding: `scripts/test-smart.sh` uses a hardcoded `BASE="${TEST_BASE_BRANCH:-origin/dev}"` default — when used on branches that diverge from `staging` or `main` (during promotions or hotfixes), the smart test will diff against `origin/dev` and may miss or over-include test files, producing a misleading "no changes" result.
recommendation: Follow the same dynamic base branch resolution pattern used in `preflight.sh` (reading `git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`) instead of hardcoding `origin/dev` as the default.

finding: `scripts/pre-push-check.sh` Gate 2 runs `pnpm run format` and if formatting changes are detected it commits them automatically with `git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null commit -m "chore: auto-format"` — this bypasses Husky and commitlint hooks, silently creates commits with a generic message, and violates the project's policy of never using `--no-verify`-equivalent bypasses.
recommendation: Remove the auto-commit behavior from the pre-push hook; instead fail the hook with a message instructing the developer to run `pnpm run format` and commit the result manually, preserving the integrity of the commit history and hook chain.

finding: `scripts/agent-verify.sh` runs `pnpm run format` (auto-fix) rather than `pnpm run format:check` (lint-only) as its first gate — running an auto-fixer in a pre-commit-equivalent script means it silently mutates files, which can produce uncommitted formatting changes if the agent does not re-stage after running the script.
recommendation: Change agent-verify.sh gate 1 to `pnpm run format:check` and document that agents must run `pnpm run format` separately and commit any formatting changes before invoking agent-verify.

finding: The Vite library config auto-discovers component entry points via `discoverEntryPoints()` scanning `src/components/hx-*/index.ts`, producing per-component ESM entry points in `dist/components/*/index.js` without requiring a manually maintained entry list — eliminating merge conflicts and omission errors when adding new components.

The Vite config correctly externalizes `lit`, `@lit/*`, `@helixui/tokens`, and `@floating-ui/*` from the component bundle, preventing Lit from being bundled into the component output and ensuring consumers use a single shared Lit instance — critical for Shadow DOM registry deduplication.

The library `dev` script is `vite build --watch` (rebuild on change) rather than `vite` (dev server with HMR) — this means the library has no true hot-module replacement in development; consuming apps (Storybook, admin) must rebuild the full library bundle on every source change, adding 2–5 seconds of rebuild latency per edit cycle.
recommendation: Evaluate whether `vite build --watch` is intentional given the library-mode constraint (not a browser app), and if so document the reasoning. Consider using a tsconfig `--watch` for type declarations alongside the Vite watch build to give faster feedback on type errors without a full build.

finding: The root CLAUDE.md documents `pnpm run dev` as the all-apps dev server start command, but neither the root `turbo.json` nor the individual package scripts include the docs app (`apps/docs`) in the default `dev` filter — `turbo dev` will start all packages with a `dev` script including Storybook and admin but the Astro docs site only starts via `pnpm run dev:docs`.
recommendation: Verify whether docs should be included in the default `turbo dev` invocation and update the CLAUDE.md quick reference table accordingly. Ensure `dev` script in docs package matches what is expected by the Turborepo pipeline.

finding: The batch test scripts in `hx-library/package.json` (`test:batch:1` through `test:batch:5`) use hardcoded component name lists in regex patterns — when new components are added they must be manually assigned to a batch or they will be excluded from batch testing entirely, silently missing CI test coverage.
recommendation: Replace static batch lists with a dynamic script that distributes discovered test files across N batches alphabetically, similar to how `discoverEntryPoints()` works in vite.config.ts — no manual maintenance required.

finding: `scripts/block-local-publish.mjs` correctly blocks `npm publish` outside CI environments by checking multiple CI environment variables (`CI`, `GITHUB_ACTIONS`, `GITLAB_CI`, `CIRCLECI`, `JENKINS_URL`) and is hooked via `prepublishOnly` — this is a solid guard against accidental local publishes.

`scripts/validate-cem.mjs` is a sophisticated CEM accuracy validator that performs per-class source analysis covering properties, events, CSS parts, and slots — including comment stripping and JS attribute selector exclusion to avoid false positives. This exceeds typical manifest validation in comparable library ecosystems.

The `hx-library` `build` script runs three sequential operations inline: `vite build && pnpm run cem && pnpm run css:build` — these are separate concerns (JS bundle, CEM generation, CSS bundle) that could fail independently, but failures in cem or css:build will produce a confusing error attributed to the `build` script with no context.
recommendation: Keep the three operations as separate Turborepo tasks (`build`, `cem`, `css:build`) with declared `dependsOn` relationships so Turborepo can report, cache, and retry each independently.

finding: The root `package.json` defines 25 `hooks:*` scripts (e.g., `hooks:lighthouse-performance`, `hooks:vrt-critical-paths`, `hooks:animation-budget-check`) that invoke tsx scripts — none of these are wired into Husky hooks, called from preflight, or referenced in CI configuration, making their purpose and execution context completely opaque and potentially dead tooling.
recommendation: Either integrate each hook script into the appropriate quality gate (preflight, pre-commit, CI) with documentation, or delete the dead scripts. Undocumented tooling creates false confidence and maintenance burden.

finding: No root-level `README.md` for the monorepo was found in the repository scan — the `CLAUDE.md` contains comprehensive agent instructions but there is no developer-facing onboarding document explaining the tech stack, local setup commands, workspace structure, or contribution workflow for human contributors or new team members.
recommendation: Create a root `README.md` with: prerequisites (Node version, pnpm version), setup steps (`pnpm install`, `pnpm run dev`), workspace overview, dev server ports, and links to each app's documentation. This should be derived from CLAUDE.md but targeted at human contributors.

finding: The `scripts/` directory contains 18 shell scripts and multiple `.mjs`/`.ts` utilities with no index or README describing their purpose, usage, or when each should be invoked — a new team member or agent has no way to discover the difference between `preflight.sh`, `agent-verify.sh`, `pre-push-check.sh`, and `pre-commit-check.sh`.
recommendation: Add a `scripts/README.md` that categorizes each script by trigger (manual, pre-commit hook, pre-push hook, CI, agent-only) and documents any required environment variables and expected exit codes.

finding: The `@helixui/tokens` package.json has a well-formed exports map with named sub-path exports (`./css`, `./lit`, `./utils`, `./tokens.css`, `./tokens.json`) covering all consumer use cases, and the `linked` changeset group ensures it versions with `@helixui/library`.

`packages/hx-library/package.json` declares `@floating-ui/dom` as a `peerDependency` but it is not listed in `devDependencies`, meaning local development and tests run without the floating-ui package installed unless a consuming app provides it — this breaks any component that uses floating-ui positioning in isolated test environments.
recommendation: Add `@floating-ui/dom` to `devDependencies` in `packages/hx-library/package.json` at the version that satisfies the peer range so tests and Storybook have the dependency available without relying on hoisting from a consuming app.

finding: There is no Turborepo remote caching configuration in `turbo.json` or the root `package.json` — for a 50+ component monorepo with 9 CI gates, local cache only means every CI run and every new developer clone pays the full cold build penalty, potentially 3–5 minutes per run.
recommendation: Configure Turborepo Remote Cache via `TURBO_TOKEN` and `TURBO_TEAM` environment variables in CI (GitHub Actions secrets) and document the setup so team members can share cache. Alternatively evaluate Vercel Remote Cache (free for open-source) given the existing Vercel deployment.

finding: The `hx-react` package has `"prebuild": "pnpm run generate"` which runs the React wrapper generator before every build — the generator reads `packages/hx-library/custom-elements.json`, but if the library hasn't been built yet (cold clone) the CEM doesn't exist and the prebuild fails silently or generates an empty wrapper set. This creates a fragile cold-start dependency that is not captured in the Turborepo pipeline.
recommendation: Remove the `prebuild` hook from `hx-react` and instead enforce the `generate` step through the Turborepo pipeline by making `hx-react#build` depend on `@helixui/library#cem` via a proper `dependsOn` in the task pipeline, so Turborepo guarantees CEM exists before generation runs.
